title: Choose the visual world for Melissia Boss Timer
question: The roll dealt the Night Tide Table. Metro Live Tiles beat it on both axes. Keep one, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Night Tide Table
options.lineage: printed tide tables and nautical almanacs, read at night
options.thesis: The day's spawns read like tides: a 24-hour crest band shows when the big ones roll in.
options.viewport: Left nav (Schedule, Bosses, Sounds, Settings); full-width 24h crest band with a now-line, crest height = boss rank; next spawn in huge tabular numerals; almanac columns of coming spawns.
options.risk: The tide band turns decorative if crest height stops meaning boss rank; nautical motifs must stay out of controls.

raised.raise: The alarm is the only event allowed to invert the window: at alarm time the field flips to its negative.
One rank only: the next spawn is the single raised surface; everything else lies flat on the ground.
One visible module: the band's hour ticks are the grid every column below aligns to.
State is marked, not tinted: passed spawns are struck through, wanted bosses carry a ring.

options.label: Match-Day Broadcast
options.lineage: LCK and esports broadcast schedule graphics
options.thesis: Every spawn billed like a match card: the fixture list, with the next one on air.
options.viewport: A NEXT UP lower-third with boss and countdown spans the top; fixtures grouped by time block below; filters and sounds in a side panel.
options.risk: Closest to the gaming-UI default; slides into neon esports cliché if the type gets timid.

options.label: Metro Live Tiles
options.thesis: Windows' own Metro language: giant lowercase boss names and a live tile for the next spawn, readable across the room.
materials: light-weight giant type cropped at the edge
options.viewport: Black ground; giant cropped boss name with the countdown in light weight; a row of flat tiles for the next spawns; boss tiles flood cyan when their alarm is on.
options.case: Wins both axes: the Xbox/Windows Metro look is gamers' own, and poster-size countdown reads from a second monitor.
options.risk: Pure black plus one accent edges toward the dark-neon rut; navigation must stay standard tabs, not a panorama.

options.label: Midnight Line Diagram
options.lineage: metro route diagrams in midnight enamel
options.thesis: The day drawn as a rail line: spawns are stations, the 4-hour regulars ride their own coloured loop.
options.viewport: A 24h line across the top with station ticks and the next station lit; spawns listed by line below; settings in a side panel.
options.case: Holds clarity: recurring loops read as lines. Loses identification for a countdown-first job.
options.risk: 32 stations a day crowd the line; the countdown becomes secondary to the map.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Spawns as a black-and-white barcode field.
options.viewport: A barcode strip of the day over dense mono columns.
options.case: Loses both: players don't identify with gallery data art, and bars hide boss names.
options.risk: Strobing is hostile beside a game.
options.kept: Full-field inversion reserved for the alarm.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Settings as tabbed manual sections under clear leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail with the schedule as the open section.
options.case: Loses both: a manual is for reading, not glancing at a countdown.
options.risk: Reads as nostalgia, not a timer.
options.kept: One rank only: a single raised layer for what matters now.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A countdown built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid numerals for the next spawn over a small grotesk list.
options.case: Loses both: players don't identify with it, and grid letterforms slow boss-name reading.
options.kept: A visible module every column aligns to.

options.label: Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Bosses as stamp-sized cells circled in biro.
options.viewport: A packed grid of boss cells with your picks circled.
options.case: Loses both: no licensed boss art to fill cells, and the grid buries the next spawn.
options.risk: Needs artwork the project can't ship.
options.kept: State marked by hand: struck through when passed, ringed when wanted.

canonCard.label: Windows 11 utility, done right
canonCard.thesis: A Fluent dark utility: Mica, Segoe UI Variable, NavigationView, one accent.
canonCard.viewport: Left NavigationView; next-spawn card on top; ListView of upcoming spawns; settings as Fluent cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other Windows utility by design.
